book_level_anchors.decision: Preserve good-news/gospel language as the controlling announcement of God’s saving action.
Preserve dikaiosynē as righteousness and the repeated God-righteousness network rather than replacing it with a single explanatory paraphrase.
Render dikaioō as set right where the forensic/restorative sense is active, with contextual exceptions such as Romans 6:7 where freed/acquitted is demanded by the death-to-slavery argument.
Preserve pistis as trust/faithfulness according to grammatical subject and context; do not flatten every occurrence to intellectual belief.
Romans 3:22 follows the project’s frozen subjective-genitive decision: through the faithfulness of Jesus Christ, for all who trust.
Romans 3:25 hilastērion = a place of atonement, preserving mercy-seat and sacrificial resonances without choosing one later atonement theory.
Preserve singular Sin as a ruling power across Romans 3–8, including reign/slavery/dominion imagery.
Preserve flesh/Spirit as contrasting spheres/orientations without treating physical embodiment itself as evil.
Preserve the Law’s multiple functions and Paul’s positive statements about it; do not paraphrase Romans as simple Law-versus-grace abolitionism.

Romans 9–11 must remain anti-supersessionist in translation: God has not rejected his people, Gentiles are grafted into Israel’s tree, natural branches can be grafted back, and God’s gifts/calling are irrevocable.
Preserve mercy as the climactic theological movement of Romans 9–11.
Preserve mutual belonging, gifts, hospitality, enemy-love, and strong/weak table fellowship as the embodied communal result of the gospel.
Preserve Jew/Gentile and Israel/nations distinctions while affirming the one Lord and universal gospel invitation.
Preserve the obedience-of-trust/faith phrase at Romans 1:5. The familiar matching phrase in the Romans 16 doxology belongs to an ancient textual tradition not present in the pinned SBLGNT main text.
